thread:
Eva: Quick heads-up — I repro'd a regression when combining fused flash-attn with 4-way tensor parallel. Latency jumps when batch/seq distribution across TP shards is uneven. Putting raw traces here.
Kai: ugh, timeline?
Eva: Happened on the latest runtime rollout (kernel selector 2.14). Repro command I used:
```
python infra/bench/run_attention.py --model gpt-medium --tp 4 --batch 24 --seq 896 --use-flash true --align-shards false
```
Eva: With align-shards=false, shard seq lengths differ (some got 896, some 896-64 after our chunking), and the fused kernel seems to mis-handle the QKV handshake across all-gather boundaries.
Ashish: Can you paste a short perf snippet from the run? numbers > sample please.
perf-bot: snapshot 2026-03-14T15:02:14Z
allgather: avg 9.8ms p95 15.2ms
allreduce: avg 11.9ms p95 20.3ms
compute(fused_flash_attn): avg 14.6ms p95 38.5ms
e2e step: 59.7ms

Eva: compare with align-shards=true:
allgather: avg 7.1ms
compute(non-fused fallback): avg 10.2ms
e2e step: 45.8ms

Eva: So two observations: 1) compute p95 for fused kernel explodes in presence of uneven tile sizes; 2) allgather waits increase because TP peers delay (handshake stalls).
Marco: Could this be the handshake ordering at shard boundary? I vaguely remember we optimized for identical shard sizes, not skewed.
Ashish: We only optimized collective start times assuming identical per-shard compute durations. If shard A finishes earlier it posts all-gather, but shard B still in a big fused kernel path and enters a slow fallback condition — causing imbalance + backpressure.
Kai: Is the fused kernel doing any internal sync that turns into a blocking op when input dims are not block-aligned? flash-attn can pad internally, but maybe our tile math triggers a slow path with additional memcopies.
Eva: Exactly. I dumped kernel queue events — when seq_len % 16 != 0 OR when shard tile count differs, the fused path switches to a 'generic' kernel that does extra sub-ops. That kernel uses a different launch config making compute > comm and increasing overlap loss.
Marco: Any stack traces / logs for the generic path? small snippet?
Eva: From device trace (shortened):
```
[GPU0] fused_flash_attn_fast      0.45ms
[GPU0] fused_flash_attn_generic  28.3ms  <-- hotspot for some shards
[GPU0] nccl_allgather            9.2ms
[GPU1] fused_flash_attn_generic  0.48ms
[GPU1] nccl_allgather            11.2ms
```
Eva: Notice the mismatch — GPU0 gets generic slow kernel.
Ashish: That explains the all-gather p95 spikes since devices post at different times. We lose comm/compute overlap.
Kai: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Add a kernel-selector check: disallow fused_flash_attn_fast if shard tile mismatch > threshold.
- Force explicit padding to next multiple of 16 at the TP boundary (align-shards true)
- Introduce a soft-sticky-batching: delay fast shards by tiny spin until slow ones reach nccl post (helps balance allgather posting times)
Marco: Sticky-batching sounds hacky but could buy time while we fix kernel variant math.
Eva: I prototyped sticky delay: add per-rank spin for up to 0.5ms if peers not ready. Result: p95 e2e drops from 59.7ms -> 48.1ms on that run.
perf-bot: micro-bench results (tp=4, batch=24, seq=896 -- 10 runs):
- baseline (no fixes): e2e p95 59.7ms
- pad-align shards: e2e p95 46.3ms
- kernel-selector disable-fast-on-mismatch: e2e p95 47.9ms
- sticky-delay(0.5ms): e2e p95 48.1ms

Ashish: Longer-term: we should make kernel-selection aware of TP shard shape distribution and prefer a uniform slow-but-stable kernel over mixed fast/slow that kills overlap.
Kai: Also need to handle flash-attn edge-case: when causal mask + padding present, the generic kernel might do extra global mem access. Add explicit fast-path guard: require seq_len%tile==0 AND no padding OR all shards pad-to-same-length.
Eva: Repro note: the bug reproduces more often for long-sequence models when chunking logic produces off-by-block leftovers.
Marco: Action items:
- Kai: add explicit kernel-selector rule + a config flag to force-fallback when mismatch (ETA 1 day)
- Ashish: implement safer pad-to-tp-boundary option in runtime that pads and communicates pad sizes before compute (ETA 2 days)
- Marco: run full regression suite across our internal models with tp=2,4,8 and report p50/p95 breakdowns (ETA 3 days)
- Eva: add unit/perf tests that simulate shard skew and verify nccl posting times (ETA 2 days)

Kai: One more thought — could we exploit NCCL collective async APIs to post allgathers early? Might be limited because kernel still needs inputs.
Ashish: If we can pre-post using CPU-based proxies maybe, but risky. Let's start with selector + pad.
Eva: I'll open a PR with the sticky-delay prototype and the reproducer script. Also attaching the small trace + perf logs to the thread.
Eva: PR: https://git.redwood/infr/attn-fallback/pull/42 : includes logs and simple benchmark harness.
Marco: Thanks. If anybody hits the repro, please tag me and @Kai. :thumbsup:
Kai: ACK, digging in now.
